answer: One agent, one licence: the national medical council signs each epoch challenge binding the agent's key to a single practising licence, re-checked against the council register every epoch. A second key claiming the same licence is rejected outright, since the council, not the claimant, holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real licences at roughly $200,000 each in medical school and training, about $200,000,000, plus a sonnet of study no script can fake — and any licence can be struck off on fraud, a zenith no attacker can dodge, leaving a lagoon of dead credentials.
